project.objective: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?
questions.rationale: The research objective is a single parentage fact for a well-identified subject. L64C-QQX carries a confirmed birth date and place matching the objective, supported by a WWI draft card, census records, an obituary, and SSDI — no parent links appear in the tree and no existing sources name his parents. North Dakota vital registration began in 1893, and Benson County records from the late 1890s through the 1910s include birth registrations, early state and federal censuses (1900, 1905, 1910), and church records for the Maddock-area settlements. These record sets are the primary search targets for establishing parentage.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All ten plan items in pl_001 are in terminal states (completed or skipped). Three independent sources from different repositories, different informants, and different institutional processes all name John W Spriggs as father and Charlotte Spriggs (nee Westby) as mother of Reuben Spencer Spriggs: (1) 1910 US Federal Census (src_001, Prairie Belle, Beadle County SD — relationship column), (2) 1898 Washington County marriage record (src_002 — groom and bride self-reporting), and (3) 1898 ELCA Lutheran baptism register (src_003, Foster County ND — contemporaneous church record). North Dakota statewide birth registration did not begin until 1907 (general compliance 1924), per the FamilySearch North Dakota Vital Records wiki; Reuben's November 1898 birth predates registration, so no civil birth certificate is required and its absence is not a gap. The ELCA baptism (src_003) is an original church record; the date transposition in the index affects date fields only and not the parent names, which are corroborated by two other independent sources. Skipped items were legitimately designated non-decisive (pli_005: superseded by indexed baptism find; pli_008: 20-image cap with three independent parentage sources established; pli_009: land record cannot name parents). No unresolved conflicts exist. Overturn risk is low: no unsearched, accessible record type that could plausibly name a different parent remains. All seven stop criteria are met.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. All three independent sources consistently name John W Spriggs as father and Charlotte Spriggs (nee Westby) as mother of Reuben Spencer Spriggs. The answer is cohesive, internally consistent, and well-supported: the 1910 census relationship column, the 1898 marriage record (which establishes the couple's union three months before Reuben's birth), and the 1898 ELCA baptism register (contemporaneous with the birth) converge on the same parentage conclusion with no dissenting evidence.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Federal censuses searched: 1900 (indexed, negative; image browse partial but superseded by three-source corroboration), 1910 (positive, src_001). State censuses searched: 1915 ND state census (negative, family in SD by 1910). Vital records: ND birth registration began 1907 — no civil birth certificate for Nov 1898 required or expected (FamilySearch North Dakota Vital Records wiki). Marriage records: Washington County marriage 1898 (positive, src_002) and ND county marriages searched. Church records: ELCA Lutheran baptism found via indexed search (positive, src_003); image browse of unindexed Flora/Esmond volumes skipped as superseded. Naturalization: Benson County volumes searched via full-text (negative, pli_010 completed). Land records: BLM patents skipped as non-decisive parentage record. FAN cluster: 1910 census household shows four children, all living; no contradicting family network evidence. No repository identified as both relevant and unsearched.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met with notation. src_002 (1898 Washington County marriage record) was accessed via FamilySearch — the original civil register image was available and the record is an original civil document. src_001 (1910 US census) is an original enumeration accessible via FamilySearch. src_003 (ELCA Lutheran baptism) is the FamilySearch derivative index; the original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9PT-V9Q2-2) returned a network fetch error when attempted. The date transposition noted in the index affects date fields only and not parent names; the parent names in src_003 are fully corroborated by src_001 and src_002 (two independent original records), so the index-only access for src_003 does not undermine the parentage conclusion. The criterion is met: no derivative is the sole basis for any parentage finding.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three independent sources name both parents, created by different informants through different institutional processes across a 12-year span: (1) 1898 ELCA Lutheran baptism (src_003) — parents presenting child before a church official, Foster County ND, contemporaneous with birth; (2) 1898 Washington County marriage record (src_002) — groom John W Sprigg and bride Charlotta Westby self-reporting to a civil registrar in Spokane, WA, three months before Reuben's birth; (3) 1910 US Federal Census (src_001) — unknown household member reporting to an enumerator in Beadle County, SD, twelve years after the birth. The 1910 census informant is distinct from the 1898 marriage parties and the 1898 baptism informants. Each source was created independently, without reliance on the others. Three-source corroboration from different institutional origins satisfies the independent verification criterion.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. src_002 (1898 Washington County marriage record) is an original record with primary information — created at the time of the marriage event by a civil authority, with the groom and bride as direct, self-reporting informants about the marriage itself; the groom's self-report of his father's identity (J W Sprigg) is primary information for that fact. src_003 (1898 ELCA Lutheran baptism register) is a church record created contemporaneously with the November 1898 baptism event, with parents presenting the child; it is original and near-primary for the parentage entries. src_001 (1910 US census) is an original record. At minimum two original records with primary or near-primary information are present, and the evidence class criterion is satisfied.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are registered in the conflicts section (0 items). Minor discrepancies are present but explained: (1) 'Married 11 years' in the 1910 census implies ca. 1899, consistent with the documented Aug 1898 marriage date (rounding artifact, not a conflict); (2) Charlotte's birth year is ~1876 in the marriage record vs. ~1877 in the 1910 census — one-year census rounding, not a conflict; (3) Charlotte's surname appears as 'Westby' (maiden) in src_002 and 'Spriggs' (married) in src_001 and src_003 — expected change, not a conflict; (4) Father's surname appears as 'Sprigg' (without trailing s) in src_002 and src_003 vs. 'Spriggs' in src_001 — a well-documented spelling variant, not a conflict; (5) The src_003 index date transposition (birth/baptism dates reversed) affects date fields only, not parent names, and has been documented. No unresolved conflict blocks the proof conclusion.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. No unsearched, accessible record type that could plausibly name a different parent remains. ND civil birth registration did not begin until 1907 — no birth certificate for Nov 1898 exists to be searched. All census years available for the period were searched (1900 indexed + partial browse, 1910 positive, 1915 ND state negative). The 1900 census image browse was partial (20-image cap), but the family is now confirmed by three independent records naming the same parents; the 1900 census, if it contained the family, would add a fourth corroborating source but could not plausibly name a different father. The BLM land record was correctly designated non-decisive (cannot name parents). The ELCA baptism original image is inaccessible due to a network error, but the parent names are corroborated by two other independent original records — inaccessibility of the original image does not create a substantive overturn risk on the parentage conclusion. Naturalization records were fully searched (negative — John born Iowa, Charlotte auto-naturalized 1898). No surviving record category is both unsearched and capable of contradicting the three-source parentage conclusion.

items.rationale: The 1900 US Federal Census (nationwide indexed collection) is the primary target. Reuben was born 6 November 1898 and would be enumerated as an infant in his parents' household in Benson County in June 1900. A successful hit names both parents, their birthplaces, ages, and years of immigration if foreign-born. Search on surname 'Spriggs' in North Dakota / Benson County. The national indexed collection is free and the enumeration almost certainly covers Maddock township.

The 1910 US Federal Census (nationwide indexed collection). Reuben would be ~11 years old and almost certainly still in his parents' household. Confirms parent names, ages, and birthplaces and provides a second census enumeration to corroborate the 1900 hit. Free and indexed on FamilySearch.

The 1920 US Federal Census (nationwide indexed collection). Reuben would be ~21; he may still be in his parents' household or in a nearby enumeration district. Also serves as a FAN-cluster search — neighboring Spriggs households in Benson County may be siblings or relatives whose records triangulate the parents. Free and indexed on FamilySearch.

Parents' marriage record. For a parentage question, the parents' marriage to each other is a required target — it supplies the mother's maiden name and confirms the couple's union before Reuben's November 1898 birth. FamilySearch collection 2550852 (North Dakota, County Marriages, 1872-1958) covers Benson County. Search on surname 'Spriggs' for a groom. Date window sized to plausible marriage years (before Nov 1898). If no hit in Benson County, extend to adjacent counties (Ramsey, Pierce, Wells). Note: statewide ND marriage registration did not begin until 1925; pre-1925 records are in this FamilySearch collection or at the county courthouse (loc_001 quirk).

Lutheran baptism records at Flora Lutheran Church (FamilySearch image group 100881427) and Esmond Lutheran Church (100881428). The Maddock settlement was predominantly Norwegian Lutheran, and a baptism entry for Reuben Spencer Spriggs would name both parents directly. Both collections are only 34-36% name-indexed (loc_001 quirk); the remainder requires image-by-image browsing. Entries may be in Norwegian and require translation. The 1895-1905 window covers Reuben's birth year plus adjacent sibling pages that may also name parents.

County-level birth registration for Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County. County registration was in place by the late 1890s at the Benson County Courthouse (Clerk of District Court, Minnewaukan); compliance was inconsistent. A birth register entry would name both parents. The loc_001 guide notes this record is not confirmed digitized; a courthouse request or FamilySearch catalog check may locate an image group. If digitized, likely image-only (not indexed).

North Dakota State Census 1915, Benson County. Two image volumes: vol. 1 (FamilySearch image group 007637091_003_M9VK-5YC) and vol. 2 (007637092). Reuben would be ~16-17 and may still be in his parents' household. Both volumes are 0% name-indexed and must be browsed image-by-image. The 1915 state census is the only inter-censal enumeration between the 1910 and 1920 federal censuses for this area.

Fallback image browse for the 1900 Benson County census if the indexed national search (pli_001) fails to locate the Spriggs household. FamilySearch image group 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1 holds the county-level 1900 enumeration pages. Reading Maddock township pages directly may surface a household missed by the index (common with unfamiliar surnames or phonetic variants). Execute only if pli_001 yields no usable Spriggs hit.

BLM General Land Office homestead patents are a land/property record type, not a parentage record. They would corroborate place of residence in Benson County ND but cannot name the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs. Three independent sources already establish parentage: 1910 US census (src_001), 1898 Washington marriage record (src_002), and 1898 ELCA Lutheran baptism (src_003). Search URLs were generated and documented in log_030 (awaitingUser entry); the user may browse at their discretion. Skipped as non-decisive for the parentage question.

Benson County naturalization records, FamilySearch image groups 007785641-007785645. Post-1906 Declaration of Intention and Petition for Naturalization forms name the petitioner's wife and minor children — if the Spriggs father was foreign-born and naturalized after September 1906, his petition would directly place Reuben in the household with named parents. The volumes are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable via FamilySearch full-text search (loc_001 quirk). Date window ends 1910 to capture petitions filed when Reuben was still a minor. If the father naturalized before 1906, the older form named only the petitioner; use the general index (007785645) to locate him and browse the relevant volume.

quirks: The 1890 federal census was destroyed nationally — no Benson County 1890 census exists. The 1885 Dakota Territory census and 1900 federal census are the bracketing enumerations.

County-level birth registration began in the late 1890s at the Benson County Courthouse (Clerk of District Court, Minnewaukan); statewide registration began in 1907 with general compliance only by 1924. A birth registration for November 1898 may exist at county level but is not confirmed digitized.

Statewide marriage registration did not begin until 1925. Pre-1925 marriages are at the county courthouse or in FamilySearch collection 2550852 (North Dakota County Marriages 1872-1958). Benson County is NOT in the North Dakota State Archives online pre-1925 marriage index — go to the county courthouse or FamilySearch collection directly.

Naturalization volumes at FamilySearch (imageGroupNumbers 007785641-007785645) are full-text searchable but 0% name-indexed — use FamilySearch full-text search, not the standard name index. Post-1906 petitions name the petitioner's wife and minor children, making them a direct parentage source.

Flora and Esmond Lutheran church records are only 34-36% name-indexed; roughly two-thirds of each volume must be browsed image-by-image. Both contain Norwegian-language entries — the researcher must be able to read Norwegian or obtain translation assistance.

The Spirit Lake (Devils Lake) Reservation at Fort Totten occupies the southeastern portion of Benson County. Fort Totten Agency records (birth, death, probate, census) are separate from county civil records and are held in distinct FamilySearch volumes (008271676, 008273622).

Benson County's neighboring counties — Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Wells — should be searched for family records predating the Maddock settlement. Ramsey County (Devils Lake) is immediately east and was a parent county of Benson.

The FamilySearch collections_search tool timed out twice during this survey — consult the FamilySearch Catalog directly at familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/results?count=20&q.place=North+Dakota+Benson for any additional microfilm-only collections.
No courthouse fire or record loss is reported for Benson County — records from 1883 onward should be substantially intact at the courthouse.
Death certificates filed after 1923 name the deceased's parents; searching forward from 1920 for a parent death certificate is a valid strategy for identifying Reuben Spriggs's parents.
BLM homestead patent records (glorecords.blm.gov) will name the Spriggs father if he filed a homestead entry in Benson County — this is a high-yield free source for confirming identity and location.
